test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 7 hours and 10 hours, respectively, and pipe C can empty the full tank in 14 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 4.5 hours. In how many hours will the remaining part of tank be filled?
solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills the tank in 7 hours.

Pipe B fills the tank in 10 hours.

Pipe C empties the tank in 14 hours.

**Concept Used:**

Time required = Capacity / Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let the capacity of the tank be the LCM of 7, 10, and 14 = 70 units.

Efficiency of pipe A = 10 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe B = 7 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe C = -5 units/hour (negative because it empties the tank)

All pipes were working together for 4.5 hours:

⇒ (10 + 7 - 5) × 4.5

⇒ 12 × 4.5

⇒ 54 units of work done in 4.5 hours

Now, the remaining work to be done = 70 - 54 = 16 units

After 4.5 hours, pipe A is closed, so now only pipes B and C are working together:

Efficiency of pipes B and C = 7 - 5 = 2 units/hour

Time required to complete the remaining 16 units of work:

⇒ 16 / 2

⇒ 8 hours

**∴ The remaining part of the tank will be filled in 8 hours.**
